title.zh: 卷472 列傳二百五十九 陆润庠 世续 伊克坦 梁鼎芬 徐坊 劳乃宣 沈曾植
title.en: Volume 472 Biographies 259: Lu Runxiang, Shi Xu, Yi Ketan, Liang Dingfen, Xu Fang, Lao Naixuan, Shen Cengzhi
title.raw: 卷472 列傳二百五十九 陆润庠 世续 伊克坦 梁鼎芬 徐坊 劳乃宣 沈曾植

sentences.zh: =陸潤庠=陸潤庠，字鳳石，江蘇元和人。

translations.literal: Lu Runxiang — Lu Runxiang, style name Fengshi, a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Runxiang, whose style was Fengshi, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父懋修，精醫，見藝術傳。

translations.literal: His father Maoxiu was skilled in medicine; see the Treatise on Arts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maoxiu was an accomplished physician; he is treated in the Treatise on Arts.

sentences.zh: 潤庠，同治十三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: Runxiang, in the thirteenth year of the Tongzhi reign, placed first in the top class of the jinshi examination and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, Runxiang took first place in the highest tier of the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，屢典試事，湖南、陝西皆再至。

translations.literal: Early in the Guangxu reign, he repeatedly supervised examinations; he went twice each to Hunan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu era he was repeatedly put in charge of examinations, visiting Hunan and Shaanxi twice apiece.

sentences.zh: 入直南書房，洊擢侍讀。

translations.literal: He entered service in the Southern Studio and was successively promoted to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Southern Studio on palace duty, he was promoted in turn to Reader.

sentences.zh: 出督山東學政。

translations.literal: He went out as educational commissioner for Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as educational commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，再遷祭酒，典試江西。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he was again promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and supervised the examination in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After his period of mourning for his father, he was again made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and put in charge of the Jiangxi examinations.

sentences.zh: 以母疾乞養歸。

translations.literal: On account of his mother's illness he asked leave to nurse her and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he asked leave to care for her and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，起補祭酒，擢內閣學士，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled to fill the post of Chancellor, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, and acted as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled as Chancellor, raised to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, and served concurrently as acting Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西巡，奔赴行在，授禮部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went on western tour, he rushed to the temporary court, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and served as lecturer for the imperial lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the two palaces went west on tour, he hurried to the traveling court, was made Vice Minister of Rites, and served as a lecturer at the imperial lecture sessions.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，管理醫局，典順天鄉試，充會試副總裁，署工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, managed the Medical Bureau, supervised the Shuntian provincial examination, served as Associate Chief Examiner of the palace examination, and acted as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Censor-in-Chief, took charge of the Medical Bureau, supervised the metropolitan provincial examination, served as associate chief examiner of the palace examination, and acted as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，充釐訂官制大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he served on the commission revising the governmental system.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed to the commission charged with revising the governmental system.

sentences.zh: 已而工部裁省，以尚書兼領順天府尹事。

translations.literal: Soon after the Ministry of Works was abolished, he as Minister also took charge of affairs as Prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Ministry of Works was cut, and as its former minister he also took on the duties of Prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 明年，授吏部尚書、參預政務大臣，謂：「捐例開，仕途雜，膺民社者或不通曉文義，因訂道府以下考試章程，試不及格者停其分發，設仕學館教習之。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and a Grand Councilor participating in state affairs, saying: "With the purchase-of-office regulations opened, the paths of officialdom grew mixed; those who received civil posts might not understand written meaning. He therefore drew up examination regulations for prefectural and subprefectural appointments and below; those who failed the test would have their assignment suspended, and an Official Learning Academy was set up to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Minister of Personnel and a councilor participating in state affairs. He said: "Once the purchase-of-office quotas were opened, official careers became a jumble, and men entrusted with local government sometimes could not even grasp written meaning. He therefore drew up examination rules for appointments at the prefectural level and below; candidates who failed would not be assigned, and an Official Learning Academy was established to train them.

sentences.zh: 」潤庠為陸贄後，嘗奏進文集，參以時事，大意謂：「成規未可墨守，而新法亦須斟酌行之。

translations.literal: " Runxiang was a descendant of Lu Zhi and once memorialized presenting his collected writings with reference to current affairs. The gist was: "Established rules may not be followed rigidly like ink on stone, but new measures must also be weighed and implemented with deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " A descendant of Lu Zhi, Runxiang once memorialized with his collected writings, relating them to current affairs. His main point was that old regulations should not be followed blindly, yet new policies also had to be applied with careful judgment.

sentences.zh: 若不研求國內歷史，以為變通，必至窒礙難行，且有變本加厲之害。

translations.literal: If one does not study the country's past history to guide adaptation, reforms will inevitably become obstructed and hard to carry out, with the harm of making bad matters worse.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one studies the nation's own history to guide change, reforms will only meet obstruction and become unworkable, and the harm will grow worse still.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，協辦大學士，由體仁閣轉東閣大學士，充弼德院院長。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he served as Associate Grand Secretary, transferred from the Hall of Embodied Humanity to the Eastern Pavilion as Grand Secretary, and became Director of the Academy of Moral Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong he served as associate grand secretary, moved from the Hall of Embodied Humanity to the Eastern Pavilion as grand secretary, and became director of the Academy of Moral Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝典學，充毓慶宮授讀，兼顧問大臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor pursued his studies, he served as instructor in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration and also as a consulting minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began his formal studies, he served as reader in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration and also as a consulting minister.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「曲阜篤生聖人之地，今新建曲阜學堂，必須闡明經術，提倡正學。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Qufu is the place where the Sage was truly born. Now that a Qufu Academy is newly built, the classics must be expounded and orthodox learning promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Qufu is the land where the Sage was truly born. With a new Qufu Academy now established, the classics must be clarified and orthodox learning upheld.

sentences.zh: 若雜聘外人，異言異服，喧賓奪主，將來聖教澌滅，亦朝廷之憂。

translations.literal: If foreigners are hired indiscriminately, with strange speech and dress, the guest will overpower the host; in time the Sage's teaching will fade away — a worry for the court as well.
translations.idiomatic: If foreigners are hired indiscriminately, with alien speech and dress, guests will drown out the host; in time the Sage's teaching will wither away, which would also be a grave concern for the court.

sentences.zh: 」又陳：「釐訂官制，宜保存臺諫一職。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "In revising the governmental system, the censorate and remonstrance offices should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged that in revising the governmental system, the censorate and remonstrance offices ought to be kept.

sentences.zh: 說者謂既有國會，不須復有言官。

translations.literal: Some say that once there is a national assembly, remonstrance officials are no longer needed.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that once a national parliament exists, remonstrance officials are no longer needed.

sentences.zh: 豈知議員職在立法，言官職在擊邪。

translations.literal: How could they know that the duty of assembly members is legislation, while the duty of remonstrance officials is to strike down evil?
translations.idiomatic: They fail to see that parliamentarians are charged with legislation, whereas remonstrance officials are charged with striking down wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 議院開會，不過三月，臺諫則隨時可以陳言。

translations.literal: The assembly meets for no more than three months, whereas the censorate and remonstrance offices may speak at any time.
translations.idiomatic: Parliament sits for only three months at a time, but the censorate and remonstrance offices may speak whenever the need arises.

sentences.zh: 行政裁判，系定斷於事後，言官則舉發於事前。

translations.literal: Administrative adjudication fixes judgment after the fact; remonstrance officials expose matters beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative review settles matters only after the fact, whereas remonstrance officials expose problems before they take hold.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲開通耳目，則諫院不可裁；

translations.literal: If the court wishes to keep its ears and eyes open, the Remonstrance Bureau cannot be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes to keep its ears and eyes open, the Remonstrance Bureau must not be cut;

sentences.zh: 諸臣欲鞏固君權，則亦不可言裁。

translations.literal: if the ministers wish to consolidate the sovereign's authority, they likewise must not speak of abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: and if the ministers wish to consolidate the sovereign's authority, they likewise must not speak of abolishing it.

sentences.zh: 即使他時國會成立，亦宜使該院獨立，勿為邪說所淆。

translations.literal: Even when a national assembly is established later, that bureau should remain independent and not be confused by heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a national parliament is later established, that bureau should remain independent and not be muddled by heterodox doctrines.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「遊學諸生，於實業等事學成而歸者，寥寥可數，而又用非所學。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Of students who study abroad, those who return having mastered practical industries and the like are exceedingly few, and even they are not employed in what they studied.
translations.idiomatic: " He also observed that of students sent abroad to study, only a handful return having truly mastered practical fields such as industry, and even they are not put to use in what they learned.

sentences.zh: 其最多者惟法政一科。

translations.literal: The largest number study only the field of law and government.
translations.idiomatic: By far the largest number study only law and government.

sentences.zh: 法政各國歧異，悉就其本國人情風俗以為製。

translations.literal: Law and government differ in every country; each is fashioned entirely according to its own customs and popular habits.
translations.idiomatic: Law and government differ from country to country; each nation fashions its system entirely according to its own customs and habits.

sentences.zh: 今諸生根柢未深，於前古聖賢經傳曾未誦習，道德風尚概未聞知，襲人皮毛，妄言改革；

translations.literal: Now these students' roots are not yet deep; they have never recited the classics of the ancient sages, know nothing of moral standards and social customs, pick up others' surface scraps, and rashly speak of reform;
translations.idiomatic: Today these students' roots are still shallow; they have never studied the classics of the ancient sages, know nothing of moral standards or social customs, pick up foreign surface scraps, and rashly talk of reform;

sentences.zh: 甚且包藏禍心，倡民權革命之說，判國家與君主為兩途，布其黨徒，潛為謀主。

translations.literal: some even harbor evil intent, advocate doctrines of popular rights and revolution, separate state and sovereign into two paths, spread their party members, and secretly serve as plotters.
translations.idiomatic: some even harbor malicious intent, preach popular rights and revolution, treat state and sovereign as two separate paths, spread their factions, and secretly act as ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 各部院大臣以為朝廷銳意變法，非重用學生不足以稱上旨，遂乃邪說诐行，遍播中外，久之必致根本動搖，民生塗炭。

translations.literal: The ministers of the various boards and courts, thinking the court was keen to reform and that only by heavily employing students could they satisfy the sovereign's intent, thus allowed heterodox doctrines and crooked conduct to spread throughout the realm; in time this would shake the foundations and bring the people to misery.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of the boards and courts, believing the court was bent on reform and that only by heavily employing returned students could they satisfy the throne, allowed heterodox doctrines and crooked conduct to spread at home and abroad; in time this would shake the foundations and bring the people to ruin.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳財用枯竭，請酌停新政，謂：「今日之害，先由於督撫無權，漸而至於朝廷無權。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on the exhaustion of revenue, asking that new policies be suspended in measured fashion, saying: "Today's harm begins with governors-general and governors lacking authority and gradually extends until the court itself lacks authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that revenues were exhausted and asked that new policies be suspended in measured steps, saying: "Today's harm begins with governors-general and governors stripped of authority and gradually extends until the court itself has none.

sentences.zh: 庫儲之困難，寇賊之充斥，猶其顯而易見者也。

translations.literal: The straits of the treasury and the filling of the land with bandits are still the most obvious signs.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury's straits and the land's filling with bandits are only the most obvious signs.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵之設也，所用皆未經歷練之學生，韜略則紙上空談，作用則徒取形式，甚至持不擊同胞之謬說。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of garrison troops, those employed are all untrained students; strategy exists only as empty talk on paper, and in practice they merely take form, some even holding the absurd doctrine of not striking fellow countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: As for the new garrison armies, those employed are untrained students; strategy is empty talk on paper, operations are mere form, and some even hold the absurd notion that one must not strike fellow countrymen.

sentences.zh: 一旦有事，督撫非但不能調遣，甚且反戈相向，其不可用明矣。

translations.literal: Once trouble arises, governors cannot deploy them and may even face them turning their weapons about — their uselessness is clear.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble comes, governors cannot deploy them and may even face mutiny — their uselessness is plain.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦鎮兵，仍取巡防隊而整理之。

translations.literal: It would be better to stop establishing garrison troops and instead take the patrol forces and put them in order.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to halt the garrison armies and instead reorganize the existing patrol forces.

sentences.zh: 審判之立也，所授皆未曾聽訟之法官，黑白混淆，是非倒置。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of courts of judgment, those appointed are all judges who have never heard cases; right and wrong are confused and inverted.
translations.idiomatic: As for the new courts, those appointed are judges who have never heard a case; right and wrong are confused and inverted.

sentences.zh: 舊時諳練之老吏，督撫不得用之，散遣州縣捕役，以緝盜責之巡警。

translations.literal: The experienced old clerks of former times cannot be used by governors; county constables are dispersed, and catching bandits is entrusted to the police.
translations.idiomatic: Experienced old clerks can no longer be used by governors; county constables are scattered, and bandit-catching is left to the new police.

sentences.zh: 巡警無能也，且不過省會及通商口岸有巡警，豈能分佈​​鄉閭？

translations.literal: The police are incompetent, and moreover they exist only in provincial capitals and treaty ports — how can they be spread through villages and hamlets?
translations.idiomatic: The police are incompetent, and they exist only in provincial capitals and treaty ports — how can they cover the countryside?

sentences.zh: 將來必至遍地皆盜，人民無可控訴。

translations.literal: In time bandits will fill the land everywhere and the people will have no one to whom they can appeal.
translations.idiomatic: In time bandits will fill the land and the people will have nowhere to turn for justice.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦審判，仍以聽斷緝捕歸之州縣。

translations.literal: It would be better to stop establishing courts of judgment and again leave hearing cases and catching bandits to the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to halt the new courts and again leave trials and bandit-catching to the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 諮議局之設也，所舉皆不諳掌故之議員，逞臆狂談，箝制當道，督撫莫能禁之。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of deliberative assemblies, those elected are all members ignorant of precedent; they indulge wild talk from imagination, constrain those in authority, and governors cannot restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the deliberative assemblies, those elected are men ignorant of precedent; they indulge reckless talk, constrain those in authority, and governors cannot restrain them.

sentences.zh: 於是藉籌款之名，魚肉鄉里，竊自治之號，私樹黨援。

translations.literal: Thus under the name of raising funds they prey on villages and hamlets, steal the title of self-government, and privately build party support.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of raising funds they prey on the countryside, seize the name of self-government, and privately build factional networks.

sentences.zh: 上年資政院開議，竟至戟手漫罵，藐視朝廷。

translations.literal: Last year when the Political Consultative Assembly opened its session, members even pointed fingers and hurled abuse, showing contempt for the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Political Consultative Assembly met last year, members even pointed fingers and hurled abuse, showing contempt for the court.

sentences.zh: 以辯給為通才，以橫議為輿論，蜩螗沸羹，莫可究詰。

translations.literal: They take glibness for talent and reckless debate for public opinion; like cicadas and boiling soup, nothing can be investigated to the end.
translations.idiomatic: They take glibness for talent and reckless debate for public opinion; the clamor is like boiling soup, and nothing can be settled.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦國會，仍以言事責之諫院。

translations.literal: It would be better to stop establishing a national assembly and again charge the Remonstrance Bureau with speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to halt the national parliament and again charge the Remonstrance Bureau with speaking on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 學堂之設也，所聘皆未通經史之教員，其沿用教科書，僅足啟發顓蒙，廢五經而不讀，禍直等於秦焚。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of schools, those hired are all teachers ignorant of the classics and histories; the textbooks they follow can only enlighten the dull-witted; the Five Classics are abandoned unread — the harm equals the Qin burning of books.
translations.idiomatic: As for the new schools, the teachers hired know neither classics nor histories; their textbooks can only instruct the ignorant; the Five Classics are cast aside unread — a calamity equal to the Qin burning of books.

sentences.zh: 暑假、星期，毫無拘束，彼血氣未定者，豈不結黨為非？

translations.literal: Summer vacation and weekly holidays impose no restraint; will those whose blood and qi are not yet settled not form parties and do wrong?
translations.idiomatic: With summer vacation and weekly holidays wholly unrestrained, will hot-blooded youths not band together for mischief?

sentences.zh: 又膳學費百倍於前，致使貧寒聰穎之士流，進身無路。

translations.literal: Moreover board and tuition fees are a hundred times what they were before, so that poor but clever scholars have no path to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Board and tuition now cost a hundred times what they once did, shutting poor but gifted scholars out of advancement altogether.

sentences.zh: 則莫如停辦中小學堂，仍用經策取士。

translations.literal: It would be better to stop establishing primary and secondary schools and again select scholars by classics and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to halt primary and secondary schools and again select officials through the classics and policy essays.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆於財政有關，而禍不僅在財政，使不早為之所，必至權柄下移，大局不可收拾。

translations.literal: All these bear on finances, yet the harm is not only financial; if measures are not taken early, authority will shift downward and the overall situation will become irremediable.
translations.idiomatic: All of this touches finances, yet the harm is not financial alone; unless dealt with early, authority will drain downward and the situation will become irremediable.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，多不報。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, most of it received no response.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, most of it went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 時建設立憲內閣，宰輔擁虛名而已。

translations.literal: At the time a constitutional cabinet was being set up, but the chief ministers held only empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a constitutional cabinet was being formed, but the chief ministers held only empty titles.

sentences.zh: 武昌兵變，官軍既克漢陽，武昌旦夕下。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang mutiny broke out, government troops had already taken Hanyang and Wuchang would fall at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang mutiny broke out, government troops had already taken Hanyang, and Wuchang was about to fall.

sentences.zh: 而新內閣又成立，總理大臣袁世凱議修和息戰禍，取隆裕太后懿旨，頒示天下，改建國體，於是遜位詔下矣。

translations.literal: A new cabinet was again formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai proposed peace to end the calamity of war, obtained an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, promulgated it throughout the realm, and changed the form of state — thus the abdication edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: A new cabinet was formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai proposed peace to end the war, obtained an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, promulgated it throughout the realm, and changed the form of government — and so the abdication edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 潤庠以老瞶辭授讀差，奉懿旨仍照料毓慶宮，給月俸如故，授太保。

translations.literal: Runxiang, on account of old age and dim sight, resigned his post as instructor; by imperial edict he was still to attend to the Palace of Accumulated Celebration, his monthly salary continued as before, and he was appointed Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Runxiang, citing old age and failing sight, resigned his post as instructor; by edict he was still to oversee the Palace of Accumulated Celebration, his monthly salary continued unchanged, and he was made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 越二年，病卒，年七十五，贈太傅，諡文端。

translations.literal: Two years later he died of illness at the age of seventy-five; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died of illness at seventy-five; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 潤庠性和易，接物無崖岸，雖貴，服用如為諸生時。

translations.literal: Runxiang's nature was easygoing; in dealing with others he had no steep barriers; though honored, his dress and use were as when he was a student.
translations.idiomatic: Runxiang was easygoing by nature and unpretentious in dealing with others; though he rose high, his dress and habits remained those of a student.

sentences.zh: 遇變憂鬱，內結於胸而外不露。

translations.literal: When change came he was inwardly troubled, knotting grief within his breast while showing nothing outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: When upheaval came he was inwardly troubled, knotting grief within while showing nothing outwardly.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，竟日危坐，瞑目不言，亦不食，數日而逝。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave he sat upright all day with eyes closed, speaking not and eating not, and after several days passed away.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave he sat upright all day with eyes closed, neither speaking nor eating, and after several days he died.

sentences.zh: =世續=世續，字伯軒，索勒豁金氏，隸內務府滿洲正黃旗。

translations.literal: Shi Xu — Shi Xu, style name Boxuan, of the Suoluohejin clan, registered with the Imperial Household under the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xu, whose style was Boxuan, was of the Suoluohejin clan and registered with the Imperial Household under the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年舉人，以議敘主事歷內務府郎中，擢武備院卿，授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he became a provincial graduate; by seniority he served as a director in the Imperial Household, rose to Director of the Armory, and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination; by seniority he served in the Imperial Household, rose to Director of the Armory, and was made Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為總管內務府大臣，兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he became Superintendent of the Imperial Household and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became Superintendent of the Imperial Household and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，各國聯軍入京，兩宮西狩，適遭父喪，命留京辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies of the various powers entered the capital; the two palaces went on western tour; he happened to be in mourning for his father and was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies entered Beijing; the two palaces went west on tour; he was mourning his father and was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 即日縗墨詣聯軍請保護宮廷​​，日為宮中備飲饌，並保壇廟。

translations.literal: That very day, in mourning garb, he went to the allied armies to request protection for the palaces; daily he prepared food and drink for the palace and also protected the altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: That very day, still in mourning garb, he went to the allied armies to request protection for the palaces; each day he arranged food for the palace and also secured the altars and temples.

sentences.zh: 晉理籓院尚書，調禮部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 兩宮回鑾，賞黃馬褂，轉吏部，兼都統。

translations.literal: When the two palaces returned, he was rewarded with a yellow jacket, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently served as banner general.
translations.idiomatic: When the two palaces returned, he was rewarded with a yellow jacket, moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently served as banner general.

sentences.zh: 內務府三旗甲米向歸吏胥代領折價，名曰「米折」，所得甚微。

translations.literal: The ration grain of the three banners under the Imperial Household had long been collected by clerks on behalf of the recipients and converted to cash at a discount, called "grain conversion," with very little received.
translations.idiomatic: Ration grain for the three banners under the Imperial Household had long been collected by clerks on the recipients' behalf and cashed out at a discount, called "grain conversion," yielding very little.

sentences.zh: 世續商之倉場，飭旗丁自領，眾感實惠。

translations.literal: Shi Xu negotiated with the granary officials and ordered banner soldiers to collect in person; the people were grateful for the real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xu negotiated with the granary officials and ordered banner soldiers to collect rations in person; the people were grateful for the real benefit.

sentences.zh: 纂呈四書圖說，特旨褒嘉。

translations.literal: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received a special edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，尋授體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as Associate Grand Secretary and soon after was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Humanity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as associate grand secretary and soon after was made grand secretary of the Hall of Embodied Humanity.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 歷轉文華殿大學士，充憲政編查館參預政務大臣。

translations.literal: He was transferred in turn to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and served as a councilor participating in state affairs on the Constitutional Research Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and served as a councilor on the Constitutional Research Bureau.

sentences.zh: 念八旗生計日艱，奏設工藝廠，俾習工藝贍身家。

translations.literal: Mindful that the livelihood of the Eight Banners grew daily harder, he memorialized to establish craft workshops so they might learn crafts to support their households.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that livelihoods in the Eight Banners grew harder by the day, he memorialized to establish craft workshops so bannermen could learn trades to support their families.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，議繼體，世續獨言國事艱危，宜立長君，不能用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong died and succession was discussed, Shi Xu alone said the state's affairs were perilous and an elder sovereign should be established; his view was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu died and succession was discussed, Shi Xu alone urged that the state was in peril and an older heir should be chosen; his view was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，以疾乞休。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign began, he asked to retire on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuantong reign began, he asked to retire on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，復起原官，仍兼總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled to his former posts and still concurrently served as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to his former posts and again served as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 及議遜位，世續首讚之。

translations.literal: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was the first to approve it.
translations.idiomatic: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was the first to endorse it.

sentences.zh: 太后令磋商優待條件，授太保。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered him to negotiate favorable terms and appointed him Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered him to negotiate favorable terms of treatment and appointed him Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 接修崇陵工程，加太傅。

translations.literal: He took charge of repairing the Chongling mausoleum project and was further made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of the Chongling mausoleum repairs and was further made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，懼禍及，力阻之。

translations.literal: In the dingsi year when restoration was attempted, fearing calamity would reach him, he strongly opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingsi year, when restoration was attempted, fearing disaster would reach him, he strongly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 事變亟，入宿衛，並以殮服自隨。

translations.literal: When the crisis came swiftly, he entered palace guard service and even carried burial garments with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis broke swiftly, he entered palace guard service and even carried burial garments with him.

sentences.zh: 頻年以經費拮据，支持尤苦，纂修德宗實錄，始終其事，及書成，已病不能起矣。

translations.literal: Year after year funds were tight and support was especially hard; he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong from start to finish, and when the book was completed he was already too ill to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year funds were tight and the strain was severe; he saw through the compilation of Emperor Guangxu's Veritable Records from start to finish, and when the work was done he was too ill to rise.

sentences.zh: 辛酉年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the xinyou year he died at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinyou year he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: =伊克坦=伊克坦，字仲平，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人，西安駐防。

translations.literal: Yi Ketan — Yi Ketan, style name Zhongping, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner stationed at garrison duty in Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan, whose style was Zhongping, was of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner garrisoned at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年進士，以編修歷至都察院副都​​御史，充滿蒙文學堂監督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi; from Compiler he rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and served as superintendent of the Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination; from Compiler he rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as superintendent of the Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 有請達海從祀文廟者，伊克坦以達海創定國書，繙譯經史，有功聖教，允宜附祀，即為代奏，略言：「學官立於漢京，而配享實始於唐代，宋、元以來，迭有增祀，大率以闡明聖學，有功經訓為斷。

translations.literal: When someone requested that Dahai be granted accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple, Yi Ketan held that Dahai had created and fixed the national script and translated the classics and histories, meriting the Sage's teaching, and should indeed be granted accompanying sacrifice; he memorialized on their behalf, stating in brief: "School officials were established in the Han capital, but accompanying sacrifice in the temple truly began in the Tang; since Song and Yuan there have been repeated additions to sacrifice, generally judged by whether one clarified the Sage's learning and had merit in the classics and instructions.
translations.idiomatic: When someone petitioned that Dahai be granted accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple, Yi Ketan argued that Dahai had created and fixed the national script and translated the classics and histories, serving the Sage's teaching, and ought indeed to receive accompanying sacrifice; he memorialized on their behalf, stating in brief: "School officials were established in the Han capital, but temple accompanying sacrifice truly began in the Tang; since Song and Yuan sacrifices have been repeatedly expanded, generally on the criterion of clarifying the Sage's learning and meriting the classics.

sentences.zh: 漢儒許慎，特因說文解字，功在經籍，專隆升祔。

translations.literal: The Han scholar Xu Shen, solely because of Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters, had merit in the classics and was specially elevated to accompanying sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Han scholar Xu Shen was specially elevated to accompanying sacrifice solely because Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters served the classics.

sentences.zh: 我太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝指授文臣創立國書，傳譯經史，宣布文教，尤極千古未有之盛。

translations.literal: Our Taizu High Emperor and Taizong Literary Emperor directed civil officials to create the national script, transmit and translate the classics and histories, and proclaim civil teaching — a splendor unmatched in a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu and Taizong directed civil officials to create the national script, translate the classics and histories, and proclaim civil culture — a splendor unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 夫國書字體，創自文臣額爾德尼及噶蓋等，而仰承聖意，匯集大成，詳定頒行者，實唯儒臣達海。

translations.literal: As for the forms of the national script, they were created by the civil officials Erdeni, Gagai, and others, but it was the Confucian minister Dahai alone who, following the sage intent, gathered the great completion, worked out the details, and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: The forms of the national script were first created by civil officials such as Erdeni and Gagai, but it was the Confucian minister Dahai alone who, following the imperial intent, brought the work to completion, worked out the details, and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 達海以肇造貞元之佐，擅閎通著述之才，歷相兩朝，瞻言百里。

translations.literal: Dahai, as an assistant at the founding of the primal order, excelled in broad and penetrating literary talent, served as chief minister through two reigns, and his words were heeded for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai, as an assistant at the dynasty's founding, possessed broad literary talent, served as chief minister through two reigns, and his counsel carried far.

sentences.zh: 其初奉命詳定國書，重加圈點，發明音義；

translations.literal: At first he was ordered to work out the national script in detail, adding dots anew and clarifying sounds and meanings;
translations.idiomatic: At first he was ordered to finalize the national script in detail, adding diacritical dots and clarifying sounds and meanings;

sentences.zh: 又以國書漢字對音未全，於十二字頭之外有所增加，而國書之用乃廣。

translations.literal: because the phonetic correspondence between the national script and Chinese characters was not complete, he made additions beyond the twelve syllabaries, and the use of the national script then broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Because phonetic correspondence between the national script and Chinese characters was incomplete, he made additions beyond the twelve syllabaries, and the script's use broadened.

sentences.zh: 复定兩字切音之法，較之漢文切音，更為精當，而國書之制乃備。

translations.literal: He further fixed the method of two-character phonetic spelling, which compared with Chinese phonetic spelling was more precise and exact, and thus the system of the national script was made complete.
translations.idiomatic: He further established the method of two-character phonetic spelling, more precise than Chinese fanqie spelling, and so the national script's system was completed.

sentences.zh: 繙譯經典，昭示群倫，功不在傳經諸儒下。

translations.literal: Translating the classics and making them known to all the people — his merit is not below that of the Confucian scholars who transmitted the classics.
translations.idiomatic: By translating the classics and making them known to the people, his merit was no less than that of the scholars who transmitted the classics.

sentences.zh: 崇德十年，既蒙賜諡文成，康熙九年，复奉賜文立碑，隆德報功，永受恩澤。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongde he was granted the posthumous name Wencheng; in the ninth year of Kangxi he again received the posthumous name Wen and a stele was erected; virtue was exalted and merit rewarded, receiving favor ever after.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chongde he received the posthumous name Wencheng; in the ninth year of Kangxi a stele was again erected in his honor; virtue was exalted and merit rewarded, and his favor endured.

sentences.zh: 旋有學士阿理瑚奏請從祀文廟，禮臣復奏，以為創造國書，一藝之長，不當從祀，未經議準。

translations.literal: Soon Scholar Alihu memorialized requesting accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple; the Ministry of Rites memorialized again, holding that creating the national script was mastery of a single art and unfit for temple sacrifice — it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Scholar Alihu petitioned for accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple; the Ministry of Rites replied that creating the national script was mastery of a single art and unfit for temple sacrifice, and the request was not approved.

sentences.zh: 查達海詳定國書字體，實禀太宗指示而成。

translations.literal: Investigation shows that Dahai's detailed fixing of the national script forms was in fact completed following Taizong's instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation shows that Dahai's finalization of the national script was in fact carried out under Taizong's direction.

sentences.zh: 作者為聖，述者為明，非唯羽翼六經，抑且昭示百世。

translations.literal: The author is sage, the expounder is enlightened; he not only winged the Six Classics but also made them known for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The author is the sage, the expounder brings clarity; he not only supported the Six Classics but proclaimed them for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 部議謂僅一藝之長，實未深知大體。

translations.literal: The ministry's deliberation called it only mastery of a single art and truly failed to grasp the larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that this was only mastery of a single art and failed to grasp the larger principle.

sentences.zh: 達海於聖經有表章之力，於後學有津逮之功。

translations.literal: Dahai had the power to expound the sage classics and the merit of providing a ford for later learners.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai had the power to expound the sage classics and provided a bridge for later learners.

sentences.zh: 方今宗學、旗學兼重國書，並奉旨特設滿蒙文學堂於京師，奉省亦經奏立八旗滿蒙文中學堂。

translations.literal: At present the imperial clan schools and banner schools all emphasize the national script; by imperial order a Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy was specially established in the capital, and Fengtian province has also memorialized to establish banner Manchu-Mongol middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial clan schools and banner schools all emphasize the national script; by imperial order a Manchu-Mongol Literary Academy was established in the capital, and Fengtian has also set up banner Manchu-Mongol middle schools.

sentences.zh: 揆諸古者釋奠祭師之誼，達海應得附祀，核與漢儒許慎從祀之例亦屬相符。

translations.literal: Measured against the ancient meaning of the libation sacrifice to teachers, Dahai ought to receive accompanying sacrifice; checked against the precedent of the Han scholar Xu Shen, it also conforms.
translations.idiomatic: By the ancient rite of honoring teachers at the libation sacrifice, Dahai ought to receive accompanying sacrifice; this also matches the precedent of the Han scholar Xu Shen.

sentences.zh: 仰懇俯準達海附祀文廟，並請敕建專祠於盛京，以昭矜式。

translations.literal: We humbly beg approval for Dahai's accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple and also request an order to build a dedicated shrine at Mukden to display a model for admiration.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg approval for Dahai's accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple and also request an order to build a dedicated shrine at Mukden as a model for admiration.

sentences.zh: 查盛京東門外尚有達海塋墓，榛莽荒蕪，碣碑剝落，並請敕下所司修治看護，用示朝廷崇尚實學、藎念儒臣之至意。

translations.literal: Investigation shows that outside Mukden's eastern gate Dahai's tomb still exists, overgrown with brambles and weeds, its stele peeling; we also request an order to the responsible offices to repair and guard it, to show the court's esteem for solid learning and deepest regard for Confucian ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Mukden's eastern gate Dahai's tomb still stands, overgrown and neglected, its stele crumbling; we also ask that the responsible offices be ordered to repair and guard it, showing the court's esteem for solid learning and regard for Confucian ministers.

sentences.zh: 又代陳典學事宜，略言：「伏讀雍正三年世宗憲皇帝諭：'帝王禦宇膺圖，咸資典學。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on behalf of others regarding canonical learning affairs, stating in brief: "I have read the instruction of the Shizong Manifest Emperor in the third year of Yongzheng: 'Emperors who rule the realm and receive the mandate all rely on canonical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on canonical learning, stating in brief: "I have read the instruction of Emperor Yongzheng in the third year of his reign: 'Emperors who rule the realm all rely on canonical learning.

sentences.zh: 我聖祖仁皇帝天亶聰明，而好古敏求，六十餘年孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Our Sagely Ancestor the Benevolent Emperor was heaven-endowed with intelligence, yet loved antiquity and pursued learning keenly, for more than sixty years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sagely Ancestor the Kangxi Emperor was heaven-endowed with intelligence, yet loved antiquity and pursued learning keenly, for more than sixty years without slackening.

sentences.zh: '又喜慶二十四年仁宗睿皇帝：'帝王之學，在於貫徹天人，明體達用，以見諸施行，與經生尋章索句者不同。

translations.literal: ' Again in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing the Renzong Sagacious Emperor: 'The learning of emperors lies in penetrating heaven and man, clarifying substance and reaching application, and making it visible in practice — different from classicists who hunt chapters and seek phrases.
translations.idiomatic: ' Again in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing the Jiaqing Emperor said: 'The learning of emperors lies in penetrating heaven and man, clarifying principle and putting it into practice — unlike classicists who hunt through chapters and phrases.

sentences.zh: '仰見列聖相承，重視典學之至意。

translations.literal: ' Thus one sees the successive sage emperors' deepest intent in valuing canonical learning.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus one sees the successive sage emperors' deepest intent in valuing canonical learning.

sentences.zh: 我皇上睿哲性成，聰明天縱，衝齡踐祚，洪業肇基，當此春秋典學之時，實為聖敬日躋之始，伏維監國攝政王薰陶德性，輔養聖躬，慎選侍從，左右將護，亦既淵衝翕受，法戒靡遺。

translations.literal: Our present emperor's sagely wisdom is innate, his intelligence heaven-bestowed; ascending the throne in tender years, the great enterprise was newly founded. At this time of canonical learning in his youth, it is truly the beginning of daily advance in sage reverence. The Regent Prince has cultivated his moral nature, assisted in nurturing the sacred person, carefully chosen attendants, and guarded him on left and right; he has already received deeply in his tender years, with models and warnings none omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Our present emperor's sagely wisdom is innate and his intelligence heaven-bestowed; ascending the throne in tender years, the great enterprise was newly founded. At this time of canonical learning in his youth, it is truly the beginning of daily advance in sage reverence. The Regent Prince has cultivated his moral nature, nurtured the emperor's person, carefully chosen attendants, and guarded him on every side; he has already received instruction deeply in his tender years, with every model and warning preserved.

sentences.zh: 唯是皇上一念之張弛，系萬機之治忽；

translations.literal: Yet whether the emperor's single thought is tight or loose bears on the diligence or neglect of ten thousand affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether the emperor's single thought is disciplined or lax bears on the diligence or neglect of all affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 一朝之規制，系薄海之觀瞻。

translations.literal: the regulations of a single court bear on the gaze of all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: the regulations of a single court bear on how all within the seas regard the throne.

sentences.zh: 有不得不慎之又慎者，謹為我皇上詳晰陳之：一，請崇聖學。

translations.literal: There are matters that cannot but be doubly cautious; I respectfully set them forth in detail for our emperor: First, I request exaltation of sage learning.
translations.idiomatic: There are matters that demand the utmost caution; I respectfully set them forth in detail for our emperor: First, I request that sage learning be exalted.

sentences.zh: 易端蒙養，禮重師教，書述遜敏，詩頌緝熙，聖學精微，非尋常科學範圍之所能及。

translations.literal: The Changes begin with nurturing the young, the Rites emphasize teachers' instruction, the Documents describe humility and diligence, the Odes praise bright harmony — sage learning is subtle and refined, beyond what ordinary branches of learning can reach.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes begin with nurturing the young, the Rites emphasize teachers, the Documents describe humility, the Odes praise harmony — sage learning is subtle and refined, beyond what ordinary branches of learning can encompass.

sentences.zh: 宋儒有言'帝王之學，與儒生異尚'，與我仁宗睿皇帝典學之諭用意正符。

translations.literal: Song Confucians said 'the learning of emperors differs in aim from that of Confucian scholars' — this matches exactly the intent of our Renzong Sagacious Emperor's instruction on canonical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Song Confucians said 'the learning of emperors differs in aim from that of scholars' — this matches exactly the intent of our Jiaqing Emperor's instruction on canonical learning.

sentences.zh: 今我皇上典學之初，應定教學科目，自應會通今古，融貫中西，不可拘於舊例。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of our emperor's canonical studies, teaching subjects should be fixed; they should naturally unite past and present and blend China and the West, and cannot be bound by old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Now at the beginning of our emperor's studies, teaching subjects should be set; they should unite past and present and blend Chinese and Western learning, and cannot be bound by old precedents.

sentences.zh: 伏乞簡派儒臣，詳細籌訂，鑑成憲，酌時宜，毋徒陳進講之空文，毋虛循延英之故事，庶足以開張聖聽，裨益亶聰，以立聖學聖治之基。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that Confucian ministers be selected and sent to plan in detail, taking established statutes as mirror and weighing the times' needs, not merely offering empty texts for lecture, not vainly following the old story of the Yanying sessions, so as to open the sage ear, benefit true intelligence, and lay the foundation of sage learning and sage governance.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Confucian ministers be selected to plan in detail, taking established statutes as guide and weighing present needs, not merely offering empty lecture texts or vainly following old Tang court rituals, so as to open the emperor's ear, sharpen his intelligence, and lay the foundation of sage learning and sage rule.

sentences.zh: 一，請擇賢傅。

translations.literal: Second, I request selection of worthy tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Second, I request selection of worthy tutors.

sentences.zh: 舊制師傅向以大臣選充，期於老成典型，成就君德，然或入官從政，講學非其所長。

translations.literal: By old regulation tutors were chosen from among great ministers, expected to be mature models and complete the ruler's virtue; yet some entered office and pursued politics, and lecturing was not their strength.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation tutors were chosen from among great ministers, expected to be mature models who would complete the ruler's virtue; yet some entered office and pursued politics, and lecturing was not their strength.

sentences.zh: 老師大儒，潛德隱而勿耀，而教育精深，尤非研究有素，不能取益。

translations.literal: Old teachers and great Confucians keep their virtue hidden and do not display it; education is profound and refined, and especially without long study one cannot gain benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Venerable teachers and great scholars keep their virtue hidden; education is profound, and without long study one cannot truly benefit from them.

sentences.zh: 擬請敕下內外大臣，各舉所知，勿拘資格，略仿乾隆十四年詔舉經學人員成例，擇其品端學粹、教育卓著成績者，請旨召用，隆以師傅之任，分門講教，而仍派大臣總司其成，俾專日講於經筵，不必更勞以職事。

translations.literal: It is proposed to order civil and military ministers within and without to each recommend those they know, not bound by qualifications, roughly following the precedent of the fourteenth year of Qianlong's edict recommending classical scholars; those of upright character, pure learning, and outstanding educational achievement should be summoned by imperial order, honored with the post of tutor, and assigned to teach by subject, while still dispatching a great minister to oversee completion, so they may devote themselves daily to the imperial lecture sessions without being further burdened with official duties.
translations.idiomatic: It is proposed to order ministers within and without to recommend those they know, without regard to formal qualifications, roughly following the Qianlong fourteenth-year precedent for recommending classical scholars; men of upright character, pure learning, and outstanding teaching records should be summoned, honored as tutors, and assigned to teach by subject, while a great minister oversees the whole, so they may devote themselves daily to the imperial lectures without other official burdens.

sentences.zh: 其任彌專，其責彌重，其效彌速，使天下曉然於尊師崇儒之意，庶儒林有所矜式，而聖德日進高明矣。

translations.literal: The more specialized the duty, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the effect; let all under heaven clearly understand the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucianism, so the Confucian grove may have a model to admire, and sage virtue daily advance to loftier heights.
translations.idiomatic: The more specialized the duty, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the effect; let all under heaven understand the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucian learning, so scholars may have a model to admire and sage virtue daily advance.

sentences.zh: 一，請肅​​規制。

translations.literal: Third, I request strict regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Third, I request strict regulations.

sentences.zh: 古者聖王教冑，必選端方正直、道術博聞之士，與之居處，是以習與智長，化與心成。

translations.literal: In antiquity when sage kings taught the imperial heirs, they always chose upright and square, straight and correct men of broad learning in the Way, to dwell with them; thus habit grew with wisdom and transformation formed with the heart.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when sage kings taught the imperial heirs, they chose upright men of broad learning in the Way to dwell with them; thus habit grew with wisdom and character formed with the heart.

sentences.zh: 我皇上毓德方新，始基宜固，舊制選派內監伴讀，似不足以肅學製而廣箴規。

translations.literal: Our emperor's nurtured virtue is newly formed and the foundation should be made firm; the old system of selecting eunuchs as reading companions seems insufficient to dignify the school system and broaden admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor's character is newly forming and the foundation should be made firm; the old system of eunuch reading companions seems insufficient to dignify the school system and broaden moral guidance.

sentences.zh: 擬請改選王公大臣之賢子弟昕夕侍從，斅學相長，並參考學校制度，建設講堂，陳列圖書彝器，觀摩肄習，以收敬業樂群之效。

translations.literal: It is proposed to change the selection to worthy sons and younger brothers of princes and great ministers to attend morning and evening, learning from each other in mutual growth, and also with reference to school systems to build lecture halls, display books and ritual vessels, observe and study, to achieve the effect of reverent work and delight in fellowship.
translations.idiomatic: It is proposed to choose worthy sons of princes and great ministers to attend morning and evening, learning from each other, and with reference to school systems to build lecture halls, display books and ritual vessels for study and observation, to achieve reverent learning and fellowship.

sentences.zh: 以上三事，僅舉大綱。

translations.literal: The three matters above present only the main outline.
translations.idiomatic: The three matters above present only the main outline.

sentences.zh: 我皇上今日之言動起居，罔有勿敬，即異日之立政敷教，罔有勿臧，此尤根本之至計，不可不謹之於漸，而慎之於始者也。

translations.literal: Our emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without what is not reverent; likewise in future establishing government and spreading teaching there will be nothing not good — this is especially the fundamental plan, which cannot but be carefully attended from the gradual beginning and cautiously handled at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without irreverence; likewise in future establishing government and spreading teaching there will be nothing amiss — this is the fundamental plan, which must be carefully attended from the start.

sentences.zh: 伏念朝廷廣勵人才，振興教育，侁侁學子，爭自濯磨，皇上典學伊始，益宜宏茲遠謨，以慰天下士民之望。

translations.literal: I reflect that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education; numerous students compete to polish themselves; as our emperor's canonical studies have just begun, it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching plan to satisfy the hopes of scholars and people throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education; countless students strive to improve themselves; as our emperor's studies have just begun, it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching plan to satisfy the hopes of scholars and people throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，伊克坦與大學士陸潤庠及侍郎陳寶琛，同奉命直毓慶宮，朝夕入講，遇事進言，憂勤彌甚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, Yi Ketan together with Grand Secretary Lu Runxiang and Vice Minister Chen Baochen were alike ordered to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration, lecturing morning and evening, speaking forth on affairs as they arose, their worry and diligence ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuantong, Yi Ketan together with Grand Secretary Lu Runxiang and Vice Minister Chen Baochen were ordered alike to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration, lecturing morning and evening, speaking forth whenever affairs arose, their worry and diligence ever greater.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，潤庠已前卒，寶琛為議政大臣，伊克坦一不爭權位，日進講如故。

translations.literal: In the dingsi year when restoration was attempted, Runxiang had already died earlier; Baochen became a deliberative minister; Yi Ketan did not contend for rank or position at all and lectured daily as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingsi year, when restoration was attempted, Runxiang had already died; Baochen became a deliberative minister; Yi Ketan did not contend for rank or position and lectured daily as before.

sentences.zh: 及事變，誓臨危以身殉。

translations.literal: When the crisis came, he vowed that facing danger he would give his body in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis came, he vowed to give his life in martyrdom if danger threatened.

sentences.zh: 伊克坦忠直有遠識，主開誠佈公，集思廣益；

translations.literal: Yi Ketan was loyal, upright, and far-sighted, advocating openness and sincerity, gathering many thoughts for broad benefit;
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan was loyal, upright, and far-sighted, advocating openness and sincerity and gathering counsel from many sides;

sentences.zh: 而左右慮患深，務趨避，時復相左。

translations.literal: but those at his side, fearing deep calamity, strove to avoid it and at times opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: but those around him, fearing disaster, strove to avoid risk and at times opposed him.

sentences.zh: 伊克坦憂鬱遂久病，日寄於酒。

translations.literal: Yi Ketan grew melancholy and then long ill, daily seeking refuge in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketan grew melancholy and fell into long illness, taking refuge daily in wine.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，卒，年五十有八，諡文直。

translations.literal: In the guihai year he died at the age of fifty-eight and was given the posthumous name Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the guihai year he died at fifty-eight and was given the posthumous name Wenzhi.

sentences.zh: =梁鼎芬=梁鼎芬，字星海，廣東番禺人。

translations.literal: Liang Dingfen — Liang Dingfen, style name Xinghai, a native of Panyu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dingfen, whose style was Xinghai, was a native of Panyu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 法越事亟，疏劾北洋大臣李鴻章，不報。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese affair grew urgent, he memorialized impeaching Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese crisis grew urgent, he memorialized impeaching Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 旋又追論妄劾，交部嚴議，降五級調用。

translations.literal: Soon after a follow-up discussion held his impeachment reckless; the matter was referred to the ministry for strict deliberation and he was demoted five ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his impeachment was judged reckless; the matter was referred to the ministry for strict deliberation and he was demoted five ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 張之洞督粵，聘主廣雅書院講席；

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhidong supervised Guangdong, he engaged him to head the lecture chair at the Guangya Academy;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong, he engaged him to head the lecture chair at the Guangya Academy;

sentences.zh: 調署兩江，复聘主鍾山書院；

translations.literal: transferred to act for Liangjiang, he again engaged him to head the Zhongshan Academy;
translations.idiomatic: transferred to act for Liangjiang, he again engaged him to head the Zhongshan Academy;

sentences.zh: 又隨還鄂，皆參其幕府事。

translations.literal: and when he returned to Hubei, in all cases he took part in his secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and when he returned to Hubei, he took part in all his secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 之洞銳行新政，學堂林立，言學事惟鼎芬是任。

translations.literal: Zhidong vigorously pursued new policies; schools stood everywhere; matters of learning were entrusted to Dingfen alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong vigorously pursued new policies; schools sprang up everywhere; all matters of education were entrusted to Dingfen alone.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，兩宮西幸，鼎芬首倡呈進方物之議。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose and the two palaces went west on tour, Dingfen was the first to propose presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer calamity arose and the two palaces went west on tour, Dingfen was the first to propose presenting local products.

sentences.zh: 初以端方薦，起用直隸州知州；

translations.literal: At first through Duanfang's recommendation he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili department;
translations.idiomatic: At first, on Duanfang's recommendation, he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili department;

sentences.zh: 之洞再薦，詔赴行在所，用知府，發湖北，署武昌，補漢陽。

translations.literal: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to proceed to the traveling court, appointed prefect, dispatched to Hubei, acted for Wuchang, and was confirmed at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to the traveling court, appointed prefect, sent to Hubei, acted for Wuchang, and was confirmed at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 擢安襄鄖荊道、按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Qian circuit, Judicial Commissioner, and acted as Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Qian circuit, Judicial Commissioner, and acted as Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏請化除滿、漢界限。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the removal of Manchu-Han distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting the removal of Manchu-Han distinctions.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，入覲，面劾慶親王奕劻通賕賄，請月給銀三萬兩以養其廉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he attended court audience and in person impeached Prince Qing Yikuang for pervasive bribery, asking that thirty thousand taels of silver be given him monthly to nurture his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he attended court and in person impeached Prince Qing Yikuang for pervasive bribery, asking that thirty thousand taels of silver be given him monthly to support his integrity.

sentences.zh: 又劾直隸總督袁世凱「權謀邁眾，城府阻深，能諂人又能用人，自得奕劻之助，其權威遂為我朝二百年來滿、漢疆臣所未有，引用私黨，佈滿要津。

translations.literal: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass the multitude, his mind is deep and obstructive; he can flatter men and can also use men; since gaining Yikuang's help, his authority has become what no Manchu or Han frontier minister in our dynasty's two hundred years has possessed; he employs private factions and spreads them through critical passes.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass all others, his mind is deep and obstructive; he can flatter and can also use men; since gaining Yikuang's support, his authority has become what no Manchu or Han frontier minister in our dynasty's two hundred years has possessed; he employs private factions and places them at every critical post.

sentences.zh: 我皇太后、皇上或未盡知，臣但有一日之官，即盡一日之心。

translations.literal: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; your servant has but one day in office and gives one day's full heart.
translations.idiomatic: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; your servant holds office but one day at a time and gives his whole heart for that day.

sentences.zh: 言盡有淚，淚盡有血。

translations.literal: When words were exhausted there were tears; when tears were exhausted there was blood.
translations.idiomatic: When words were exhausted there were tears; when tears were exhausted there was blood.

sentences.zh: 奕劻、世凱若仍不悛，臣當隨時奏劾，以報天恩」。

translations.literal: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, your servant will memorialize impeachment at any time to repay heaven's grace."
translations.idiomatic: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, your servant will memorialize impeachment at any time to repay heaven's grace."

sentences.zh: 詔訶責，引疾乞退。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 兩宮升遐，奔赴哭臨，越日即行，時之洞在樞垣，不一往謁也。

translations.literal: When the two palaces passed away, he rushed to mourn at the bier; the next day he departed; at the time Zhidong was in the Grand Council and did not go once to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the two palaces passed away, he rushed to mourn at the bier and left the next day; at the time Zhidong was in the Grand Council and did not go once to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 明年，聞之洞喪，親送葬南皮。

translations.literal: The next year, hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the burial to Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the burial to Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 及武昌事起，再入都，用直隸總督陳夔龍薦，以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang affair arose he again entered the capital; on Zhili Governor-General Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank capital official awaiting confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang affair arose he again entered the capital; on Zhili Governor-General Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank capital official awaiting confirmation.

sentences.zh: 旋奉廣東宣慰使之命，粵中已大亂，道梗不得達，遂病嘔血。

translations.literal: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong Pacification Commissioner; Guangdong was already in great disorder, the roads blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong Pacification Commissioner; Guangdong was already in chaos, the roads were blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.

sentences.zh: 兩至梁格莊叩謁景皇帝暫安之殿，露宿寢殿旁，瞻仰流涕。

translations.literal: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to pay respects at the hall where Emperor Jing temporarily rested, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall, gazing up in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to pay respects at the hall where Emperor Guangxu temporarily rested, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall, gazing up in tears.

sentences.zh: 及孝定景皇后升遐，奉安崇陵，恭送如禮，自原留守陵寢，遂命管理崇陵種樹事。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoding Jing passed away and was laid to rest at Chongling, he respectfully escorted her according to ritual, volunteered to remain and guard the mausoleum, and was then ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaoding passed away and was laid to rest at Chongling, he respectfully escorted her according to ritual, volunteered to guard the mausoleum, and was then ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.

sentences.zh: 旋命在毓慶宮行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration.

sentences.zh: 丁巳復辟，已臥病，強起周旋。

translations.literal: In the dingsi year when restoration was attempted, he was already bedridden but forced himself up to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingsi year, when restoration was attempted, he was already bedridden but forced himself up to attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 事變憂甚，逾年卒，諡文忠。

translations.literal: The crisis grieved him deeply; more than a year later he died and was given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis grieved him deeply; more than a year later he died and was given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: =徐坊=徐坊，字梧生，山東臨清州人，巡撫延旭子。

translations.literal: Xu Fang — Xu Fang, style name Wusheng, a native of Linqing prefecture in Shandong, son of Governor Yan Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fang, whose style was Wusheng, was a native of Linqing in Shandong, son of Governor Yan Xu.

sentences.zh: 少納貲為戶部主事。

translations.literal: In youth he purchased office and became a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he purchased office and became a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法陷諒山，延旭逮問，下刑部獄。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu the French took Lang Son; Yan Xu was arrested for questioning and sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Guangxu the French took Lang Son; Yan Xu was arrested for questioning and imprisoned in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坊侍至京師，入則慰母，出則省延旭於獄，橐饘之事，皆自任之，布衣蔬食，言輒流涕。

translations.literal: Fang attended him to the capital; entering he comforted his mother, going out he visited Yan Xu in prison; matters of carrying food in bags he undertook himself; in plain cloth and vegetables he ate, and when he spoke tears always flowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fang accompanied him to the capital; at home he comforted his mother, abroad he visited Yan Xu in prison; he undertook all matters of bringing food himself; he wore plain cloth and ate simply, and tears flowed whenever he spoke.

sentences.zh: 延旭戍新疆，未出都卒，坊扶柩歸葬，徒行泥淖中，道路嘆為孝子。

translations.literal: Yan Xu was banished to Xinjiang but died before leaving the capital; Fang escorted the coffin home for burial, walking on foot through mud, and travelers on the road praised him as a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xu was banished to Xinjiang but died before leaving the capital; Fang escorted the coffin home for burial, walking on foot through mud, and travelers praised him as a filial son.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，奔赴西安行在。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he rushed to the traveling court at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he rushed to the traveling court at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 明年，扈駕返，以尚書榮慶薦，超擢國子丞。

translations.literal: The next year he escorted the imperial return; on Minister Rongqing's recommendation he was specially promoted to Deputy Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he escorted the imperial return; on Minister Rongqing's recommendation he was specially promoted to Deputy Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 鄂變起，連上五封事，俱不報。

translations.literal: When the Hubei mutiny arose he submitted five sealed memorials in succession; none received response.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hubei mutiny arose he submitted five sealed memorials in succession; none received a response.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，遂棄官。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict was issued, he then abandoned office.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication edict was issued, he abandoned office.

sentences.zh: 旋命行走毓慶宮，坊已久病，力疾入直。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration; Fang had long been ill but forced himself despite illness to enter duty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration; Fang had long been ill but forced himself to report for duty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，諡忠勤。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was given the posthumous name Zhongqin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died and was given the posthumous name Zhongqin.

sentences.zh: =勞乃宣=勞乃宣，字玉初，浙江桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Lao Naixuan — Lao Naixuan, style name Yuchu, a native of Tongxiang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Naixuan, whose style was Yuchu, was a native of Tongxiang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，以知縣分直隸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi and was assigned as county magistrate to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as county magistrate in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 查淶水禮王府圈地，力請減租蘇民困。

translations.literal: Investigating the enclosed estates of the Prince of Li's mansion in Laishui, he strongly petitioned to reduce rent and relieve the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating the enclosed estates of the Prince of Li's mansion in Laishui, he strongly petitioned to reduce rent and relieve the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，初任臨榆，日晨起坐堂皇治官書，啟重門，民有呼籥者，立親訊之，使閽者不能隔吏役，吏役不能隔人民。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, on first taking office at Linyu, each day at dawn he sat in the main hall handling official documents; when the heavy gates were opened and the people called out, he immediately heard them in person, so gatekeepers could not separate clerks and runners, nor could clerks and runners separate the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu, on first taking office at Linyu, each day at dawn he sat in the main hall handling official business; when the gates opened and people called out, he heard them in person, so gatekeepers could not block clerks from the people, nor clerks block the people from him.

sentences.zh: 其後居官二十餘年皆如之。

translations.literal: In more than twenty years of holding office thereafter he was always the same.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years of office thereafter he did the same.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃督師山海關，檄司文案。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guoquan commanded troops at Shanhaiguan, he was ordered to handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guoquan commanded troops at Shanhaiguan, he was ordered to handle documents.

sentences.zh: 歷南皮等縣，畿輔州縣遇道差，咸科於民有定額，而官取其贏。

translations.literal: He served in Nanpi and other counties; in metropolitan prefectures and counties when traveling officials passed through, all were levied on the people at a fixed quota, while officials took the surplus.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Nanpi and other counties; in metropolitan counties when traveling officials passed through, fixed levies were imposed on the people while officials took the surplus.

sentences.zh: 乃宣任蠡縣，值謁陵事竣，贏支應錢千餘緡，儲庫備公用。

translations.literal: When Naixuan served in Li county, when the tomb-visiting affair ended the surplus of disbursements amounted to more than a thousand strings of cash, stored in the treasury for public use.
translations.idiomatic: When Naixuan served in Li county, after the tomb-visiting duties ended the surplus of disbursements amounted to more than a thousand strings of cash, which he stored in the treasury for public use.

sentences.zh: 任完縣，購書萬餘卷庋尊經閣。

translations.literal: Serving in Wan county, he purchased more than ten thousand volumes of books and stored them in the Hall of Honored Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Wan county, he purchased more than ten thousand volumes of books and stored them in the Hall of Honored Classics.

sentences.zh: 任吳橋，創裡塾，農事畢，令民入塾，授以弟子規、小學內篇、聖諭廣訓諸書，歲盡始罷。

translations.literal: Serving in Wuqiao, he founded village schools; when farm work ended he ordered the people to enter the schools and taught them the Rules for Students, the Inner Chapters of the Elementary Learning, the Amplified Imperial Instructions, and other books, stopping only when the year ended.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Wuqiao, he founded village schools; when farm work ended he had the people enter the schools and taught them the Rules for Students, the Elementary Learning, the Amplified Imperial Instructions, and other books, stopping only at year's end.

sentences.zh: 先是寧津奸民陳二糾黨為州郡害，土人稱曰黑團，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: Earlier in Ningjin the wicked commoner Chen Er gathered a party to harm the prefecture and counties; locals called them the Black Band, and their power was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Ningjin the wicked commoner Chen Er gathered a gang to terrorize the region; locals called them the Black Band, and their power was very strong.

sentences.zh: 嘗至南皮劫殺，乃宣會防營掩捕，擒陳二及其黨數人磔於市，黑團遂絕。

translations.literal: They once came to Nanpi to rob and kill; Naixuan joined the defense camp in a surprise arrest, seized Chen Er and several of his party, and dismembered them in the market; the Black Band was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They once came to Nanpi to rob and kill; Naixuan joined the defense camp in a surprise arrest, seized Chen Er and several of his followers, and executed them in the market; the Black Band was thus extinguished.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，義和拳起山東，蔓延於直、東各境，乃宣為義和拳教門源流考，張示曉諭，且申請奏頒禁止，不能行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Boxer Fists arose in Shandong and spread through Zhili and the eastern regions; Naixuan wrote An Investigation of the Origins of the Boxer Fist Teaching Sect, posted it for public instruction, and also petitioned that prohibition be memorialized and promulgated — it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Boxer Fists arose in Shandong and spread through Zhili and the east; Naixuan wrote An Investigation of the Origins of the Boxer Teaching, posted it for public instruction, and petitioned that prohibition be memorialized and promulgated — it could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 景州有節小廷者，匪首也，號能降神。

translations.literal: In Jing prefecture there was Jie Xiaoting, a bandit chief who claimed he could summon spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing prefecture there was Jie Xiaoting, a bandit chief who claimed he could summon spirits.

sentences.zh: 乃宣飭役捕治，縱士民環觀，既受笞，號呼不能作神狀，梟示之，匪乃不敢入境。

translations.literal: Naixuan ordered runners to arrest and punish him, allowing scholars and commoners to surround and watch; after he received the bastinado he cried out but could not perform the spirit state; he was displayed by decapitation, and the bandits then dared not enter the district.
translations.idiomatic: Naixuan ordered runners to arrest and punish him, allowing scholars and commoners to watch; after the bastinado he cried out but could not perform his spirit act; he was executed and displayed, and the bandits then dared not enter the district.

sentences.zh: 明年，拳黨入京，乃宣知大亂將作，適調吏部稽勳司主事，遂請急南歸，浙撫任道鎔延主浙江大學堂。

translations.literal: The next year the Boxer party entered the capital; Naixuan knew great disorder would break out; he happened to be transferred as director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Review Bureau, then asked to hurry south and return home; Zhejiang Governor Ren Daorong engaged him to head the Zhejiang University.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Boxers entered the capital; Naixuan knew great disorder was coming; he had just been transferred to the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Review Bureau, asked to hurry south, and Zhejiang Governor Ren Daorong engaged him to head Zhejiang University.

sentences.zh: 尋入江督李興銳幕，端方、周馥繼任，咸禮重之。
